title: Mixed lag models matched a small-target model in 54 network summaries but gave a full response at equilibrium
abstract: A prior study used fast and slow slopes of community thermal composition to infer a small response at equilibrium rather than a long lag. We tested its one-rate assumption. We used the published climate emulators and slope estimates for the same 54 networks with positive spatial slopes. A mixture of positive response rates with weights that sum to one had a fit score of 286.90, compared with 287.38 for the small-target model and 325.57 for the one-rate full-target model. Held-out network scores for the mixture and small-target model were 313.51 and 313.03. A two-rate full-target model gave similar results with two fitted parameters. The mixture put 76% of its response at the lowest tested rate, with a half-life of 231 years. This boundary value is not a measured recovery time. We prove that, without a lower bound on rates, a full-target model can approach a small-target model arbitrarily closely on any finite bounded climate record. Low tracking remains supported. The claim that it mainly reflects a small response at equilibrium does not follow from this lag test. The analysis uses published summaries, fixed spatial slopes and a common linear mixture; it does not establish a slow ecological cause.

display.caption: Fit scores from 54 network summaries, fitted response weights, and synthetic unit-step responses. The positive-rate mixture has a full target. Future curves are illustrations, not forecasts.

citations.reason: We reuse its published network summaries and climate emulators. Mixed response rates challenge its inference that long lags do not explain the gap; low observed tracking is unchanged.
